title: Enterprise Chatbot Platform
subtitle: Design an internal ChatGPT that 40,000 employees choose over consumer tools, with every turn re-authorised, permission-filtered and audited.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Result, bars and discovery
practice_prompts.hint: Name the egress result, both bars, and the questions that change the build.

practice_prompts.label: Sizing and cost
practice_prompts.hint: Derive turns, open streams and tokens per minute; say what binds first.

practice_prompts.label: Architecture and permissions
practice_prompts.hint: Order the turn by dependency and show where scope intersection and fail-closed checks run.

practice_prompts.label: Failure drills
practice_prompts.hint: Walk the laundromat, injection, stale revocation and provider outage through detect, contain, recover, prevent.

practice_prompts.label: Rollout and metrics
practice_prompts.hint: Give phases, measured gates and the metrics each audience reads.

rubric: Frames the goal as displacing consumer-AI egress, with governance and adoption held together.
Raises build versus buy before being asked and defends a hybrid.
Sizes on 800 concurrent streams via Little's Law and names provider TPM as the binding limit.
Re-authorises every turn and derives retrieval permissions from the asking human.
States effective assistant scope as assistant scope intersected with viewer permissions.
Treats index ACLs as a pre-filter and drops chunks whose live ACL cannot be resolved.
Scans streamed output with overlapping windows and finalises, meters and audits every turn path.
Rolls out one risk class per phase on measured gates, reading block rate with false-positive rate.

editorial_review.evidence: Read all 48 captured sections of the chatbot platform source and rewrote them into the five-section shell. Tutorial parts 1-8 became eight walkthrough steps; the quadratic-history and unit-cost material, records/endpoints, the turn-handler code, three of the four failure drills with the pytest boundary tests, and the Item 17/18 coverage-notes gaps became five deep dives. The worksheet and model answer are interleaved in Practice so each worksheet prompt precedes its model-answer reveal; the four mock prompts had no source answers, so their reveals are assembled from the case and labelled as worked examples, as is the users-and-workflows answer. Repetition consolidated: the 60-second version, key takeaways and the answer-key architecture restate the walkthrough, so they map to existing passages rather than repeating. Added definitions (egress, live permissions, SSO, ACL, TTFT, DLP, works council, query-time resolvable, legal hold, SLO, p95, RPO, SSE, fail closed, game day) and arithmetic steps (57,600/hour, 40x41/2=820, 4.6M/320/6,400). Invented figures (board/on-call quotes, impact statement) keep the source's invented label; $22 keeps the beta-measurement caveat. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): answer key's week 0-8 rollout vs the tutorial's weeks 1-23+ phases → the four-phase schedule (Alpha 1-6, Beta 7-14, GA 15-22, assistants 23+), because the phase table, the phases figure and the 'plain chat within six weeks' decision all use it; worksheet's 'one corpus' → 'the first corpora', matching the Beta's two corpora.
